after: Clause (a) is [[lem-em-rectangular-transverse-mode-completeness]](b) instantiated at the cross-section, whose profiles are those of the candidate theorem. Clause (b) is the rectangular reflection-class lemma [[lem-em-rectangular-pec-energy-completeness]] read physically, as packaged in [[thm-em-waveguide-spectral-completeness]](b): the class, the first-order system, density of finite separated modes, unique $C_tL^2$ weak solutions and constant energy all come from that supplier; the identification of the energy with $\int_Qu$ uses $D=\varepsilon E$, $B=\mu H$ and [[pthm-em-restricted-material-energy]](a), and the macroscopic equations follow from the two evolution equations together with the distributional divergence constraints of the class. For the scalar basis distinction in (a), every nonconstant Neumann product is orthogonal to $h_{00}=1$, and the complete orthogonal expansion of [[lem-em-rectangular-transverse-mode-completeness]] shows that deleting that one basis element gives precisely its orthogonal complement, the zero-mean subspace. The constant scalar element remains in the full basis and is excluded only as a monochromatic TE reconstruction. In (b), the explicit weak first-order model is solved by [[lem-em-rectangular-pec-energy-completeness]] as packaged in the wrapper; its Fourier energy proof gives the quadratic energy conservation without applying a smooth-only local balance to rough fields. For (c), [[thm-em-waveguide-spectral-completeness]] supplies the spectral and smooth-eigenfield assertions and the associated wave at the positive parameter $v_{\mathrm{wave}}=(\varepsilon\mu)^{-1/2}$, with its exact arbitrary $V\times H$ initial-data interface, displacement $C_tV$ and velocity $C_tH$. To derive the first-order coefficient equations, prove the actual curl pairing against each smooth PEC eigenfield $u_j$, not an unproved equality of electric and magnetic boundary classes. A smooth normal collar of the compact boundary exists by [[thm-euclidean-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem]]. Write $s$ for the inward normal coordinate (its gradient is the negative extended unit normal) and use the standard smooth step [[def-the-standard-smooth-step-function]] to set a cutoff $\eta_\delta=0$ for $s\le\delta$ and $1$ for $s\ge2\delta$. The normal tube has bounded Jacobians on the compact collar. Since $n\times u_j=0$ on the boundary and $u_j$ is smooth, $|n\times u_j|\le Cs$ in the collar. Thus $\eta_\delta u_j\to u_j$ and $\operatorname{curl}(\eta_\delta u_j)\to\operatorname{curl}u_j$ in $L^2$: the derivative-cutoff term is bounded on a layer of volume $O(\delta)$ because $|\nabla\eta_\delta|\le C/\delta$ and its cross product with $u_j$ is $O(s/\delta)$. For every $F\in H(\operatorname{curl})$, the distributional identity on the compactly supported smooth test $\eta_\delta u_j$ is $\langle\operatorname{curl}F,\eta_\delta u_j\rangle=\langle F,\operatorname{curl}(\eta_\delta u_j)\rangle$. Cauchy-Schwarz and the two $L^2$ limits give $\langle\operatorname{curl}F,u_j\rangle=\langle F,\operatorname{curl}u_j\rangle$. Apply this only to $F=B(t)$, which has the stated actual graph regularity. Then $a_j'=v_{\mathrm{wave}}^2\langle B,\operatorname{curl}u_j\rangle$. The assumed $B\in C^1_tL^2$ permits one further scalar derivative, giving $a_j''=v_{\mathrm{wave}}^2\langle B',\operatorname{curl}u_j\rangle=-v_{\mathrm{wave}}^2\langle\operatorname{curl}E,\operatorname{curl}u_j\rangle=-v_{\mathrm{wave}}^2\lambda_j\langle E,u_j\rangle$ by the full-$X$ eigenvariational identity of [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]], since $E(t)\in V\subset X$. No second time derivative of the whole field is assumed. If $\lambda_j=0$, that identity tested at $u_j$ gives $\operatorname{curl}u_j=0$, so the preceding formula for $a_j'$ is zero. Such electric zero modes are constant under first-order Maxwell evolution, while the associated unrestricted second-order equation retains affine zero modes. Divergence constraints and the declared magnetic normal condition remain part of the physical model; the pairing does not impose a magnetic electric-type trace. The inherited AC and AComega assumptions cover the spectral/Fourier and collar suppliers. No lossy or open-domain step is made.
